# WaveFern: full wiki

> Every page of the WaveFern Wiki (https://wavefern.com/wiki/) as plain text, for game v49.19.0. WaveFern is a free music career game (a 3D open-world music career sim) that you play in your browser at https://wavefern.com/.

---

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/first-day/

Your first day
From the WaveFern Wiki
New career
Cash	$100
Energy	100
Home	Starter house
Phone	Gphone 8
Tutorial gift	$150 + small rewards

You start as an unknown artist with $100, a starter house with a tiny studio and a laptop. The goal: record songs, release them on Spotifly, and grow from nobody to a global star.[1]

Your bedroom on day one: the bed, the wardrobe and the computer desk.
Gameplay
Pick an artist name on the laptop (E at the desk, then Spotifly). You cannot record until you have one.
Walk to the mic in your studio and press E. Pick a genre and play the three recording minigames. Each song costs 15 energy.
Back at the laptop, open Spotifly › Upload, give the draft a title and release it. Streams start right away.
Sleep in your bed to end the day. Overnight, yesterday's Streams are paid out and your monthly listeners update.
Spend the money on Studio gear so your next songs are better, and repeat.
The tutorial

Big Vee, your manager, walks you through the first steps. Each step pays a little cash and each chapter a bit more:

Chapter	Step	Goal
1	Find your feet	Walk around. Hold Shift to sprint.
1	Pick a stage name	Laptop (E) > Spotifly: choose your artist name.
1	Cut a track	Mic in the studio (E): pick a genre, beat four mini games.
1	Drop it	Laptop > Spotifly > Upload: release your song.
2	Check your DMs	Open Messages on the laptop.
2	Upgrade the rig	Gearshop on the laptop: buy something cheap, like Headphones ($120).
2	Fresh drip	Browser > Clothes (Threadz): buy any piece, from $12.
2	Put it on	Wardrobe in your bedroom (E): wear it.
2	Touch grass	Walk out the front door.
2	Sleep it off	Go to bed (E) when it is night or you are out of energy.
3	Know your world	Press N for the map. Scroll or +/- to zoom.
3	Wheels and fame	Listen to Big Vee.
3	Book a gig	Open FestivalApp on the laptop.
3	Back it up	Esc > Settings > Get save code. Keep it safe.
RewardsEvery step pays $3, every chapter $10, and finishing the whole tutorial $20 more. You can skip it from the pause menu, and you still get the $150 starting gift.
Early goals
Record a few songs in one genre family: the genre focus bonus rewards a steady sound.
Buy a better microphone first: it gives the most quality per level.
Install Instagrime and post once a day for followers.
Reach 10 monthly listeners to unlock your first mentor.
Screenshots
The character creator at the start of a new career.
Tips
Your first songs will not be great. That is normal: keep making them.
Sleep before 06:00, or you will start the next day tired.
See also

Streams

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/controls/

Controls
From the WaveFern Wiki

WaveFern plays with a keyboard and mouse, or with touch controls on phones and tablets.[1]

Key	What it does
WASD / arrows	Walk
Shift	Sprint (uses stamina)
E / Space / Enter	Interact: doors, desks, shops, people, mic
F	Storage and furniture build mode at home
R	Rotate furniture while placing it
N	World map (and the taxi)
M	Mute music
G	Open your phone
B	Emote wheel in a band room
Esc	Pause menu: settings, save, quit
123	Pick a rhyme in the Lyrics minigame
Space (hold)	Raise the level in the Mix minigame
Walking and stamina

You walk at 3.3 m/s and sprint at 6.5 m/s. Sprinting drains stamina by 15 per second; it refills at 10 per second when you stop. If you run it to zero you are winded and can't sprint again until it is back to 30.

Touch

On a phone or tablet a joystick appears bottom left, with buttons for sprint and interact. Menus, the phone and the computer work by tapping.

References
^ 07-input-loop.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
^ 154-touch-controls.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/days/

Days, time and energy
From the WaveFern Wiki
A game day
Real time	12 minutes
Starts	06:00
Night	20:00 to 06:00
Pass out	06:00, with 70% energy
Song cost	15 energy

A full in-game day lasts 12 real minutes, from 06:00 to 06:00 the next morning. About nine songs fit in one day.[1]

The clock

The first half of the day runs from 06:00 to 20:00; the second half is night, from 20:00 to 06:00. The clock keeps running while the computer or phone is open.

Energy
You wake with 100 energy after sleeping in your bed.
Recording a song costs 15 energy (7.5 for your part in a collab). A festival set costs 15 and a tour show 25.
Energy slowly comes back by itself during the day, about 36 over a full day.
Food tops it up: the corner shop, City Cafe, Goober Eats and festival stalls.
Sleeping

You can only go to bed at night (after 20:00), or earlier if your energy is under 15. Sleeping ends the day: yesterday's streams are paid, your monthly listeners are updated, every genre's hype is rerolled and new messages arrive.

Passing outIf you are still awake at 06:00 you pass out where you stand and wake with only 70 energy.
What happens overnight
Streams for the day are completed and paid at the stream rate (after any label cut).
Interest decays by 10% and gains 6% for each song you released that day.
Monthly listeners and followers update (followers grow by 5% of the day's streams).
Genre hype rerolls between ×0.8 and ×1.3.
A new mentor may unlock, artists may DM you, labels may make offers, and new quests roll.
See also
Food and energy
Monthly listeners and followers

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/saves/

Saves and careers
From the WaveFern Wiki

The main menu has two career slots. Each career saves on its own, so nothing leaks between them.[1]

The main menu, where you pick a career slot.
How saving works
The game autosaves to your browser as you play.
Sign in with Google from the main menu to keep your career in the cloud and play it on any device.
The pause menu can export a save code (starts with FW3-). Paste it back in to load it anywhere. Older FW2- and FW1- codes still load.
If a save ever fails to load it is kept as a recoverable backup instead of being lost. Backups show under Recovered backups on the career screen: press Recover, or drag one onto a slot.
Band careersBand rooms keep a separate band career for each room, on your device. It never touches your two career slots or your cloud save.
References

^ 86-google-signin.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/recording/

Recording a song
From the WaveFern Wiki
Recording
Where	The mic in any studio
Energy	15
Needs	An artist name
Steps	Beat · Lyrics · Mix
Time	About 80 seconds

Walk to the mic and press E to open Make a song. Pick a genre (and, if you like, extras), then play three short minigames. How well you play decides a big part of the song's quality.[1]

The Make a song screen.
The Make a song screen
A grid of the 9 genres. A genre marked HOT has hype above ×1.12 today and earns more streams; COLD is below ×0.92.
Each genre shows its genre focus percentage: how much your fans will reward (or punish) that choice.
An Extras drop-down holds the diss track, 808 and hi hat options. See Extras: diss tracks, 808s and hi hats.

Every step starts with an animated 3, 2, 1, GO countdown; nothing counts until it is over.

1. Beat

A marker swings along a bar. Hit it when it is inside the green zone (within 8% of the centre). Six good hits finish the step. Each hit speeds the marker up by 5%. You get three goes: every miss uses one, and running out scraps the take.

2. Lyrics

Pick the word that rhymes with the one shown (keys 1-3 or tap). There are five lines and the game adapts to you:

Level	Difficulty	Time per line	Traps
Easy	under 0.35	about 8 s	any other word
Tricky	0.35 to 0.7	about 5-6 s	words that look like the answer
Hard	0.7 and up	down to 3.5 s	longer rhymes, near-rhymes as traps

The time limit is 8 − 4.5 × difficulty seconds. A right answer is worth 0.85 + 0.3 × difficulty points, so harder lines count for more. Half your level carries over to the next session.

3. Mix

Hold Space (or hold the mouse) to raise the level, let go to drop it. The level rises at 1.15 per second and falls at 0.95. Keep it within 0.1 of the moving green band for 6 seconds.

mix score = min(1, time in band ÷ 6 s × 1.15)
Session grade
Average of Lyrics and Mix	Grade
0.9 and up	Studio magic
0.7 to 0.9	Solid session
0.45 to 0.7	Rough around the edges
below 0.45	Messy take

The finished draft waits on your laptop. Give it a title and release it from Spotifly › Upload, or use Upload all to release every titled draft at once.

BandsIn a band room the middle step depends on your instrument: only vocalists rhyme. Guitar, bass, drums and keys play their own part.
Screenshots
The Beat step.
The Lyrics step.
The Mix step.
Tips
Do not rush the Beat step. A clean run with no misses adds more than you would think.
The Lyrics step gets harder as you get better at it. Harder lines are worth more, so it evens out.
In the Mix step, small taps keep the level steadier than long holds.
See also
Extras: diss tracks, 808s and hi hats
Song quality
Genres and genre focus
Band rooms
References

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/song-quality/

Song quality
From the WaveFern Wiki

Every song gets a quality score. Quality drives almost everything: daily Streams, the chance of a hit, Park Fields Festival crowds and Gramophone Awards.[1]

The formula
quality = max(3, round( experience × (
    random 8-14
  + 16 × session            (average of Lyrics and Mix, 0-1)
  + gear points             (see below)
  + 3 if you own a home      + 1 per pet you own
  + 2 per unlocked mentor
  + max(0, 8 − misses)       (Beat step)
)))
Experience

New artists don't get full value from their gear. Experience starts at 0.3 and climbs towards 1:

experience = 0.3 + 0.7 × (1 − e^(−xp / 200))
xp = songs made + 8 per mentor + 6 per fame level

xp	Experience
0	0.30
25	0.38
50	0.45
100	0.58
200	0.74
400	0.91
800	0.99

Gear points

Each level of a piece of gear adds a fixed number of points (level 0 = the starting item):

Gear	Points per level	Max level	At max
Chair	4	3	12
Microphone	8	3	24
Guitar	6	3	18
Keyboard	3	3	9
Drums	3	3	9
Acoustics	5	3	15
Headphones	2	3	6
Audio interface	3	3	9
Studio monitors	3	3	9
Pedalboard	2	3	6
Bass guitar	3	3	9
Sampler	3	3	9
Vocal chain	3	3	9
Synths	3	3	9
Room treatment	3	3	9
Desk	5	3	15

Promo, decks and the content kit don't add quality; they add reach instead.

Collab songs

A collab's quality uses a different recipe: a random 30-40 base plus gear, times experience, plus up to 25 points from the fee you agreed (more for a bigger fee) and ±4 per point of opinion from the meeting chat.

Band songs

A band song's quality is the average of every member's take, plus 3 for each extra member.

Tips
Early on, making lots of songs is how you get better. Experience grows with every song.
Spend on the gear that gives the most quality per level first.
Things that stay with you for good (mentors, a home, pets) add up over a career.
See also
Streams
Park Fields Festival
Gramophone Awards
Studio gear
Collabs, fees and haggling
References

Genres and genre focus
From the WaveFern Wiki
Genres
Genres	9
Families	4
Hype range	×0.8 to ×1.3
Focus range	about −25% to +40%

There are 9 genres. Each has its own beat styles, its own daily hype, and belongs to a family of similar sounds.[1]

Genres and beat styles
Genre	Family	Beat styles
Hip-Hop	Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B and Latin	Boom Bap, Jazz Rap, G-Funk, Soul Chop, Southern Bounce, Breakbeat
Rap	Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B and Latin	Trap, UK Drill, NY Drill, Rage, Plugg, Phonk
Pop	Pop and Country	Dance Pop, Synth-pop, Pop Ballad, Tropical, Bedroom Pop, Disco Pop
Rock	Rock	Garage Rock, Punk, Arena Rock, Hard Rock Riff, Indie Rock, Grunge
R&B	Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B and Latin	Slow Jam, Neo-Soul, Trap Soul, New Jack Swing, Alt R&B, Afro R&B
Lo-fi	Lo-fi and Electronic	Chillhop, Jazzhop, Rainy Day, Lo-fi Bossa, Sleepy, Tape Beat
Country	Pop and Country	Train Beat, Honky Tonk, Country Ballad, Country Pop, Bluegrass, Country Trap
Electronic	Lo-fi and Electronic	House, Techno, Trance, Drum & Bass, Dubstep, Synthwave, Future Bass
Latin	Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B and Latin	Reggaeton, Latin Trap, Bachata, Salsa, Cumbia, Latin Pop
Hype (trending)

Every morning each genre's hype is rerolled between ×0.8 and ×1.3. It multiplies the daily streams of every song in that genre, old ones included. On the Make a song screen a genre above ×1.12 shows HOT and one below ×0.92 shows COLD.

Genre focus

Fans reward a steady sound. When you release a song, the five songs you released before it decide its focus, a multiplier it keeps on its daily streams for good.

share = (1 per same genre + 0.8 per same family) ÷ 5 previous releases
run   = how many of your latest releases in a row are in this family (max 5)
focus = 0.75 + 0.5 × share + 0.03 × run
Your last five releases	Focus
All in other families (genre hopping)	×0.75 (−25%)
Mixed, about half the same family	about ×1.0
All the same family, different genres	×1.30
All the same genre, a run of 5	×1.40 (+40%)

The families are:

Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B and Latin: Hip-Hop, Rap, R&B, Latin
Pop and Country: Pop, Country
Rock: Rock
Lo-fi and Electronic: Lo-fi, Electronic
NoteYour very first release has nothing to compare against, so its focus is ×1. A toast tells you when a release gets +5% or more, or −5% or less.
TipPick one family and stay in it for most of your releases. You can still switch: the penalty fades as your last five releases fill up with the new family.
Tips
Pick a family you like and stick with it for a while. Hopping between sounds costs you.
A HOT genre is a nice bonus for one day. It is not worth breaking a long run in your family for.
If you want to switch sound, do it gradually through a genre in the same family.
References
^ 02-data.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
^ 166-genre-focus.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
^ 67-beats.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Extras: diss tracks, 808s and hi hats
From the WaveFern Wiki

Open Extras on the Make a song screen to choose a diss track, your 808 and your hi hats.[1]

808 and hi hats

Both pickers offer Auto (the genre's own pick), Built-in (the classic synthesised sound) or one of the named samples. Your choice is remembered for the next song and saved with each song, so it plays the same every time. They change how the song sounds, not its quality.

808s (17)

Amen Cactus Camp Daffy Dime Episode Flo Glaze Grief Notebook Owl Robin Shiver Shoe Snowhurt Thin Vessel

Hi hats (9)

Aisle Business Crusade Fin Guard Meta Rooftop Turkey Utter

Diss tracks

Tick Diss track and pick a rival to make a song called No Love For [rival]. Releasing it is a gamble:

On release, interest changes by somewhere between −8% and +25%.
2 to 5 days later the rival answers. That moves interest by −12% to +20% and your reputation by −2 to +3.

See Rivals for the list of rivals.

See also
Rivals

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/streams/

Streams
From the WaveFern Wiki
Streams
Pay per stream	$0.05
Paid	Every morning
Night speed	×2
Hit chance	about 8%
Viral chance	about 0.03%

Every released song earns streams every day. Streams build up through the day (twice as fast at night) and are paid the next morning at $0.05 per stream, minus any label cut.[1]

Daily streams
daily = quality × 0.36 × random(0.75-1.25)
      × genre hype                         (×0.8-1.3, rerolled daily)
      × age decay   (0.86^days + 0.015)
      × fame        1.5^fame tier × (1 + min(1, √listeners ÷ 200))
      × interest    0.3 + 0.7 × interest
      × reach       1 + promo×0.3 + decks×0.2 + content kit + home×0.1
      × quality     clamp((quality ÷ 50)^0.8, 0.45, 2.5)
      × collab      (feature)² × (1 + 0.5 × min(1.5, quality ÷ 100))
      × focus       genre focus (see Genres)
      × 1.5 on release day

On top of that, a collab brings the featured artist's fans: about 1% of their monthly listeners a day, decaying the same way.

Other boosts that stack on top: Promotions, album tracks, the catalogue halo, your Gphone model and Radio and TV slots.

Interest

Interest is a 0-100% measure of how much people are talking about you. Each morning it drops by 10%, then gains 6% for every song you released yesterday. Albums, radio and diss tracks also move it. Releasing steadily keeps it high.

Whether a song is a hit, goes viral or is normal is rolled once, on its release day.

Hits
hit chance = 0.08 × clamp(quality ÷ 60, 0.5, 1.6)
a hit streams ×3-6
Going viral
viral chance = 0.0003 × min(1, quality ÷ 90)^3
a viral song gets 5M + listeners × 20-50 extra streams over 14 days
The cap

So one song can't run away forever, daily streams are capped:

cap = quality² × 25 × 1.5^fame tier × hit multiplier
Payouts

Each morning you're paid yesterday's streams × $0.05. If you're signed, the label keeps its cut first. Earnings show on the morning summary and in Spotifly › Stats.

Tips
Release often. Interest fades every day you do not put something out.
A song does most of its streaming in its first few weeks, so a steady flow beats one big drop.
Quality lifts everything else in the formula, so it is the best place to spend effort.
See also
Record labels
Collabs, fees and haggling
Promotions
Albums
Catalogue halo
Gphone
Radio and TV

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/listeners/

Monthly listeners and followers
From the WaveFern Wiki

Monthly listeners are the headline number: they set your Fame levels level, who DMs you, which Record labels want you, and how big your Park Fields Festival crowds are.[1]

Monthly listeners

A month is 30 in-game days. Each month the game picks a random divisor from 2 to 5. Every morning:

base = max(this month's streams, last 30 days of streams) ÷ divisor
if you had streams yesterday:
  listeners = max(base, old + yesterday ÷ (divisor × 30) + old × 1% × releases × interest)
otherwise:
  listeners = base

So while songs are streaming, monthly listeners never drop from one day to the next. When a new month starts with a bigger divisor, the number can fall.

Followers

Followers grow by 5% of each day's streams, plus extras from Instagrime posts, photo posts (bigger with a better Gphone), Radio and TV, Promotions, Park Fields Festival sets, tour shows and landmark selfies.

Tips
The monthly number can drop at the start of a new month. Keep releasing and it climbs back.
Followers come mostly from streams, so they follow the same advice.
See also
Fame levels
Collabs, fees and haggling
Record labels
Park Fields Festival
Instagrime

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/albums/

Albums
From the WaveFern Wiki

Once you have at least two released songs you can bundle them into an album from Spotifly. Pick the tracks, the order, a title and cover art.[1]

What an album does
Releasing an album adds 20% interest.
For the first 14 days, track 1 gets up to +60% streams and the other tracks up to +25%. The boost fades over those two weeks.
Albums show on your Spotifly artist page.
TipPut your best song as track 1: it gets the biggest boost.

Collabs, fees and haggling
From the WaveFern Wiki
Collabs
Started by	You, or a DM from them
Energy	7.5
Song tag	(feat. NAME)
DMs a day	0-2, max 3 waiting
Artists	128 in the game

A collab is a song with another artist. You either pay them (you messaged them) or they pay you (they messaged you). Their fans come along: a featured song gets about 1% of their monthly listeners in extra streams each day.[1]

Who messages you

Each day 0 DMs (20%), 1 (40%) or 2 (40%) can arrive, never more than 3 waiting. On your first day 2-3 small artists say hello. Who writes depends on size:

Artists about your size are the most likely.
A bit smaller: common. Much smaller: rare, unless you worked together before or share a genre.
Bigger: falls off fast with the gap, helped by your growth this week, your interest and your reputation.
Your recent genres: ×1.6 for the same genre, ×1.25 for a related one, ×0.85 otherwise.
Artists with 50k+ listeners only DM you once you have 25k. Panic Man Dan waits until you have 5,000.
The price
what they charge = their fee × size factor × markup × reach × repeat × reputation
  size factor = 0.18 + 0.82 × A ÷ (A + 1500)        (A = their listeners)
  markup      = 0.92 to 1.12, fixed per artist
  reach       = ((A + 5) ÷ (you + 5))^0.2, kept within 0.75 to 1.35
  repeat      = ×0.92 if you've worked together before
  reputation  = −1% per point (up to −10%)
what they pay you = 55% of your own market price, never more than 80% of their fee
Haggling

Type your offer in Messages in plain words, like "how about $120?", "two fifty" or "1.5k". Artists counter, and bigger names usually move less on price. A lone "100" means "keep it 100", not an offer.

The meeting

Once you agree, press Confirm & pay (or Accept & get paid). The artist waits at the meeting place (gold beacon). Walk up to them to chat for 1-3 exchanges: pick a tone (hype, chill, pro, joke, cocky) that suits their personality (chill, hype, shy, formal, goofy). Their opinion goes from −3 to +3 and changes the song: ±4 quality and ±12% feature strength per point.

feature strength = (1.05 + min(0.3, fee ÷ 6000)) × (1 + opinion × 0.12)
Artists

The game's own made-up artists. The game also has stand-ins for well-known real artists, which are left out of this list.

Tips
Pay attention to how an artist talks before you pick a tone in the meeting. A tone that suits them goes a long way.
If an artist barely moves on price, do not waste rounds lowballing them.
Artists who message you pay you. Saying yes to a few early on is easy money and new fans.
The feature is worth more when the song itself is good, so do not spend big on a collab you rush.

Promotions
From the WaveFern Wiki

From Instagrime you can pay to promote a released song. The price grows with your monthly listeners. A promoted song streams its multiplier times its normal amount every day of the campaign, and you gain followers when it starts.[1]

Promotion	Days	Streams	Price	Followers
Boost	3	×1.5	$40 + $0.002 × listeners	3-12 + 1% of listeners
Campaign	5	×2	$150 + $0.006 × listeners	3-12 + 2% of listeners
Blitz	7	×3	$600 + $0.015 × listeners	3-12 + 4% of listeners
TipA promotion multiplies the song's normal daily streams, so it is worth most on a strong, fresh song in a HOT genre.
References
^ 83-promotions.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
Category: Music

---

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/halo/

Catalogue halo
From the WaveFern Wiki

When your monthly listeners jump (after a hit or a viral song, say), some of those new fans dig into your older songs, so nothing in your catalogue is stuck at a few hundred streams.[1]

extra daily streams per song = listeners × 0.08 ÷ max(10, songs − 1)
                                × quality factor × age factor × (0.5 + 0.5 × interest) × random(0.75-1.25)
age factor = 0.4 + 0.6 × 0.985^days since release

Because it's split across the catalogue, the total stays about the same however many songs you have. Hit and viral songs don't get it. It does nothing early on, when your listeners are small.

References
^ 108-catalogue-halo.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Spotifly
From the WaveFern Wiki

Spotifly is where your music lives. Open it on the laptop (or the Spotifly app on your phone).[1]

A new artist page on Spotifly.
Setup: pick your artist name. You need one before recording.
Upload: title drafts and release them, one by one or all at once.
Stats: streams, earnings and listeners by day, and per-song history.
Artist page: your profile, top 5 songs by popularity (or all songs), albums.
Browse: other artists' pages.
Promote songs (Promotions) and build Albums.

Money
From the WaveFern Wiki

You start with $100. Most of your income comes from streams, paid every morning.[1]

Earning
Source	How much
Streams	$0.05 per stream, paid each morning (minus a label's cut)
Collabs they pay for	What you agree in Messages
Festival sets	$0.08 × stage multiplier × crowd, after every song
Tour shows	Tickets sold × (ticket price × 0.05 + 1)
Signing with a label	A one-off advance
Quests	Daily and weekly rewards
Autographs	A small tip when a fan stops you
Tutorial	$150 gift plus small step rewards
Spending

Studio gear · Collabs, fees and haggling · Promotions · Radio and TV · Cars and the garage · Homes · Furniture and storage · Clothes (Threadz) · Barbershop · Pets · Bodyguards · Jewellery · Food and energy · phones · Computer and apps · Flights and the airport · World Tour

CarefulCarrying lots of cash in the street can get you robbed. See Fans and robbery.
Tips
Buy things that make every future song better before things that only look good.
Do not walk around with all your cash once you are famous.

Fame levels
From the WaveFern Wiki
Fame
Levels	350
Level 275	62.04M listeners
Level 350	1.3B listeners
Tiers	12

Your fame level comes from your monthly listeners. Jewellery makes you look more famous: each piece adds 8%.[1]

fame value = monthly listeners × (1 + 0.08 × pieces of jewellery)

Listeners needed per level, on a log scale, level 1 to 350.

Mentors
From the WaveFern Wiki

There are 5 mentors, each inspired by a music legend. One unlocks each time you reach the next monthly listener milestone, and every mentor adds +2 quality to every song (and 8 experience). Meet them on the laptop under Legends.[1]

Mentor	Monthly listeners	Their advice
Mentor 1	10	Perfectionism and showmanship: rehearse until it feels effortless.
Mentor 2	40	Own your sound: learn every instrument in the room.
Mentor 3	120	Write honest songs. A plain story lands harder than a fancy one.
Mentor 4	400	Obsess over the mix. Details make the record.
Mentor 5	1000	Experiment fearlessly with tone and texture.
References

Record labels
From the WaveFern Wiki
Labels
First offer	Day 5
Offer chance	20% a day
Same label again	After 20 days
Leave fee	30% of advance
After leaving	No offers for 14 days

Labels message you with an offer when your monthly listeners, total streams and reputation all reach their thresholds. Signing pays an advance up front; from then on the label keeps a cut of your streaming income every night.[1]

Label	Quality	Listeners	Total streams	Reputation	Advance	Cut
Discount Discs
We sign anyone. Fast contract, no fuss, small print included.	★☆☆☆☆	300	5,000	any	$400	35%
QuickFlip Records
Quick releases, quick cash. We move units, you move on.	★☆☆☆☆	1,500	40k	any	$1,500	30%
Brickyard Sound
An honest independent label with a proper studio and a small team.	★★★☆☆	6,000	250k	0	$8,000	22%
Northlight Records
A respected label with real radio contacts and a pro production crew.	★★★☆☆	20k	1.2M	1	$40,000	20%
Meridian Music Group
A major. Top producers, global marketing and a PR machine.	★★★★☆	80k	6M	3	$250,000	16%
Crown & Anchor Records
The biggest name in music. Legendary studios, worldwide campaigns, the best team money can buy.	★★★★★	300k	30M	5	$1,500,000	12%
Rules
Offers start on day 5, once you have released a song. Each day there is a 20% chance one eligible label writes; the same label waits 20 days before asking again.
Only one offer is open at a time.
Leaving a label costs 30% of the advance you got, and no label writes for 14 days afterwards.
Label HQLabel HQ is coming soon. It is planned as the home for everything about being signed to a label. Offers, advances and cuts already work through Messages.
Tips
The first labels to call are the weakest deals. Waiting for a better label can pay off.
A label takes its cut every single night, so a big advance is not always the better deal over time.
Keep your reputation up: the best labels will not look at you without it.
References
^ 101-economy-labels.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
^ 106-label-hq-soon.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Quests
From the WaveFern Wiki

The Quests app (preinstalled on the laptop) gives you 3 daily quests and 3 weekly quests. Finish the whole set to get paid. Quests are rolled once and saved, so reloading never changes them.[1]

The quest log.
daily reward  = $30 × 1.04^fame level   (rounded to $5)
weekly reward = 10 × the daily reward
Fame level	Daily set	Weekly set
0	$30	$300
10	$45	$450
25	$80	$800
50	$215	$2,150
100	$1,515	$15,150
150	$10,770	$107,700
200	$76,520	$765,200
275	$1,449,740	$14,497,400
350	$27,465,660	$274,656,600
Daily quests
Record 2-4 songs (more at fame 10 and 30)
Release 1-3 songs
Release a song at or above your recent average quality + 3
Post on Instagrime
Send 4 messages
Walk or run 400-700 m
Weekly quests
Get 35% more streams than last week
Earn 35% more from music than last week
Gain 35% more followers than last week
Release 5-9 songs
Record 12-18 songs
Release 3 songs at your recent average quality + 6
Release an album
Post on Instagrime on 5 different days
Walk or run 3,000-6,000 m

Weeks run day 1-7, 8-14 and so on. The night after a day still counts for that day, so overnight streams land in the right week. Each set never has two quests of the same kind.

References
^ 133-quests.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/awards/

Gramophone Awards
From the WaveFern Wiki
Gramophone Awards
Needs	Fame Level 225
Cooldown	15 days
Category	Song of the Year
Prize	Gramophone Trophy

The awards hall stands at the end of your street. From Fame Level 225 you can check in (once every 15 days), submit one song, and watch the ceremony.[1]

The red carpet outside the awards hall.
How to win

You're up against four of 16 big stars, and only the single best song wins. The judges look mostly at how good your song is, with a small bonus for how many streams it has.

Tips
Submit your best song, not your newest one.
Quality matters far more than streams here. A great song with few plays beats an average song with millions.
The stars you face are very good. If you lose, keep improving your gear and come back in 15 days.
Mentors, a home and pets all add quality, so they help here too.

A win puts a Gramophone Trophy in your Storage: furniture that isn't sold anywhere.

References
^ 110-awards.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/reputation/

Reputation
From the WaveFern Wiki

Reputation is a hidden score that starts at 0.[1]

What changes it
Event	Change
A rival answers your diss track	−2 to +3
Cancelling a festival booking less than 2 days before	−2
Missing your festival slot	−3
Selfie with an artist on a Gphone 12 or newer	+1
What it does
Collab fees: 1% cheaper per point (up to 10%).
DMs: 3% more likely per point, and bigger artists reach out more.
Bigger Record labels need a minimum reputation.
See also
Record labels

Park Fields Festival
From the WaveFern Wiki
Park Fields Festival
When	Every 7th day
Where	The field east of Park Avenue
Book	FestivalApp, 2+ days ahead
Set	Up to 4 hours
Energy	15 per set
Pay per song	$0.08 × stage × crowd

A festival opens on every day that is a multiple of 7 (day 7, 14, 21...). The day before, a crew builds it; the day after, they take it down.[1]

A set at The Pit on a festival day.
Stages
Stage	Fame level	Pay	Base crowd	Max crowd
Fresh Fern Tent	10	×1.25	160	450
The Pit	61	×1.5	1,000	3,000
Riverside Stage	131	×1.75	5,000	12,000
Main Stage	225	×2	20,000	60,000
Crowd and pay
crowd = min(max, base × 1.055^(your level − stage level))
        × (0.9 + min(0.2, average quality ÷ 400))  × 1.15 for a collab song
pay after each song = $0.08 × stage multiplier × crowd
streams   = crowd × 0.1   × (0.5 + minigame score)
followers = crowd × 0.015 × (0.5 + minigame score)
Crowd minigames

Short games pop up between songs. Score 75% or more and the crowd grows; under 50% and people leave.

Minigame	Prompt
hype	Hype the crowd!
drop	Hit the drop!
call	Call and response!
lyric	Finish the line!
hold	Hold the note!
Food and drink

Festival stalls charge about 1.4× normal prices. Food gives energy; drinks also refill stamina.

Stall	Type	Menu (price / energy)
Big Stack Burgers	van	Cheeseburger $12 / +16
Double Stack Burger $18 / +24
Loaded Fries $9 / +11
Crepe Escape	van	Lemon & Sugar Crepe $8 / +10
Chocolate & Banana Crepe $11 / +14
Strawberry Crepe $11 / +14
Taco Loco	van	Three Tacos $13 / +18
Loaded Nachos $10 / +12
Churros $7 / +8
Candyfloss Cart	cart	Candyfloss $6 / +6
Giant Candyfloss $9 / +9
Popcorn Cart	cart	Salted Popcorn $5 / +6
Toffee Popcorn $7 / +8
The Field Bar	bar	Fizzy Lemonade $5 / +4 · stamina
Iced Tea $5 / +4 · stamina
Cola $4 / +4 · stamina
Berry Mocktail $8 / +6 · stamina
Bolt Bull Energy $9 / +12 · stamina
Bottle of Water $3 / +2 · stamina
Tips
Book the biggest stage your fame allows. The crowd and pay grow fast with stage size.
Put your best songs in the setlist. The crowd notices quality.
Arrive at the stage a little early so you do not miss your slot.
References

^ 71-festival-booking.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/festival-app/

FestivalApp and bookings
From the WaveFern Wiki

FestivalApp is free and installed for you. Pick a festival, a stage your fame allows and a free slot.[1]

FestivalApp, for booking a slot.
Slot	Time
Slot 1	10:00 to 14:00
Slot 2	14:00 to 18:00
Slot 3	18:00 to 22:00
Slot 4	22:00 to 02:00
Book at least 2 days before the festival. Booking is free.
Other acts have already taken some slots; at least one per stage is always left free.
Build a setlist from released songs and whole albums. Each song lasts 30-55 in-game minutes, so 4-8 songs fill a slot. The setlist can't go over 4 hours.
Editing or cancelling is free while the festival is 2+ days away. Cancelling later costs 2 reputation.
On the day, be at your stage's steps during your slot. Miss it and the slot is given away, and you lose 3 reputation.
References
^ 71-festival-booking.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
Category: Live and touring

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/flights/

Flights and the airport
From the WaveFern Wiki
Swiftwing Airways
Flights	One a day per route
Departures	07:00 to 23:30
Book	Up to 3 days ahead
Refund	70% if cancelled 2h+ ahead
Gates	1 to 6

Swiftwing is the game's airline. Book from the Swiftwing app (computer or Gphone) or at the ticket desk in any airport. Fernfield International is at the far west end of Fern Road.[1]

Booking a flight in the Swiftwing app.
Fares and flight times
flight time = max(2, round(km ÷ 800 + 0.7)) hours
fare        = round((180 + km × 0.11) ÷ 10) × 10, varying a little day to day
The rules
Step	When
Book	Until 60 minutes before departure, up to 3 days ahead
Check in	24 hours to 45 minutes before (app or a check-in desk)
Security	Needs a boarding pass
Boarding	Opens 2 hours before at the gate
Gate closes	10 minutes before departure: the ticket is lost
Cancel	More than 2 hours before, for a 70% refund
The flight

At your gate press E at the door, take your marked seat and the plane leaves. The clock moves on by the flight time. A flight that runs past 06:00 counts as your night's sleep.

TipStranded abroad with no money? Swiftwing gives you a free seat home.
Screenshots
The airport entrance.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/world-tour/

World Tour
From the WaveFern Wiki
World Tour
Unlocks	Fame Level 275
Price	$250,000 once
Stops	Up to 5
Songs per stop	Up to 12
Venue cooldown	14 days
Shows	One a day

The World Tour app appears in the App Barn at Fame Level 275. It costs $250,000 once. Plan on its world map: click a continent, then a country, then add its stops, up to 5. Each stop gets a setlist (songs or a whole album). Then book Flights and the airport and fly there.[1]

How a show pays
fill       = clamp(0.55 + 0.012 × levels above the venue's + 0.25 × preparation, 0.3, 1)
attendance = capacity × fill × (0.7 + 0.3 × show score)
money      = attendance × (ticket price × 0.05 + 1)
followers  = attendance × 0.12 × (0.5 + score)
streams    = attendance × 18   × (0.5 + score)   (to the songs you played)
Destinations

Every destination has a stadium (or big venue) and a club. Home is UTC−5.

Tips
Rehearse before big shows. It costs a little energy and makes a real difference.
Learn how to greet each crowd. Talking to them well lifts the whole show.
Production costs a lot at first, so save it for the stadiums.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/tour-shows/

Stadium and club shows
From the WaveFern Wiki

In each tour city the stadium is on the plaza and the club downtown. Walk in, plan the show in the dressing room, then play it.[1]

Before the show
Setlist: starts from your World Tour plan for that stop, or your top songs. The last song is the encore.
Rehearse up to 2 times a day: you need 20 energy and it uses 8.
A show needs 25 energy and must start between 12:00 and 02:00.
Production
Stadium extra	Price
Pyro and fireworks	$25,000
Lasers	$12,000
Confetti finale	$6,000
Dancers	$15,000
Club extra	Price
Lasers	$1,500
Confetti finale	$600
Smoke and strobes	$400
Show score
score = 0.12 + 0.5 × minigames + 0.18 × crowd hype + 0.1 × song quality + 0.05 × rehearsals (max 2) + production

Between songs you talk to the crowd. Greeting them in the local language works best (+0.16 hype). A stadium show has an intermission and an encore and runs 6-10 in-game hours.

References
^ 151-tour-shows.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.

Tour cities
From the WaveFern Wiki

Every destination becomes a city you can walk around when you land: signs in the local language, its own colours and traffic, an airport, a hotel, shops, a club and a stadium.[1]

Landmark selfie: once a day per city, for 30 + √listeners × 0.25 followers and an Instagrime post.
Hotel: check in at reception and sleep in your room. You wake up there.
Shops: restaurants, cafés, convenience stores, souvenir shops (postcards, snow globes, T-shirts, fridge magnets) and record shops.
Street food

Food stalls sell local dishes by language. Drinks also refill stamina.

The city and the map
From the WaveFern Wiki

Your house sits on a quiet street west of the city. Press N for the map: scroll or +/− to zoom.[1]

A street in town.
Places

Home Garage Jewellery Property Corner shop Maple Lane Central Park Lake West suburb South suburb Radio City Plaza City Centre Pulse Records HQ Aurora Residences Nova Mall Motors Pet Shop Security Skyline Tower Gramophone Awards City Cafe Music Store Barbershop Airport Festival ground

Taxi

From the map you can call a taxi to any place. You get one trip a day: one ride out, then one ride back to where it picked you up. After that it's gone until tomorrow.

Weather

Each day rolls its weather: Sunny, Rain, Fog, Thunderstorm. About 90% of days are sunny, 5% rain, 3% fog and 2% storms. Day 1 is always sunny.

Fans, autographs and robbery
From the WaveFern Wiki

The more famous you are, the more people recognise you. A passer-by notices you with a chance of monthly listeners ÷ 5,000,000.[1]

Autographs

Sign and you usually get a tip: $3-12 × your fame tier (at least ×1).

Robbery

Some "fans" are thieves. A robbery can only happen when you sign an autograph: instead of a tip, they grab 35% of the cash you're carrying and run.

Guards with you	Fans let through	Thief chance
0	all	5%
1	50%	2.5%
2	10%	0.5%
3	none	0%

Messages and Big Vee
From the WaveFern Wiki

Messages holds every chat: artists who DM you (see Collabs, fees and haggling), label offers and Big Vee, your manager. Pin chats to keep them on top, clear them, or press New for suggested people.[1]

The Messages app with a few DMs from other artists.
Big Vee

Big Vee is pinned by default. Text a question in plain words and Big Vee answers from your current save. Topics: controls, making a track, uploading and money, Spotifly, billboards, height, collabs, Messages, gear, clothes, sleep and energy, the map and cars, festivals, fame and saving.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/band-rooms/

Band rooms
From the WaveFern Wiki
Band rooms
Players	Up to 4
Needs	Google sign-in
Rooms	Up to 2 band careers
Host	The room creator
Emotes	Press B

From the main menu pick Multiplayer: create a room, or join one with a friend's code. A room is a band of up to 4 players who live in the starter house together.[1]

Instruments
Instrument	Their recording step
🎤 Vocals	Lyrics
🎸 Guitar	Riff
🔊 Bass	Groove
🥁 Drums	Drums
🎹 Keys	Melody

You pick your instrument the first time you join, and keep it for that band career. Everyone spawns in the studio, which has every member's instrument.

How it works
Each member has their own band career for that room, saved on their own device. It never touches your solo careers or cloud save.
The host's clock is the band's clock. Only the host's bed ends the day.
Recording and festival sets need every online member present and ready.
Band songs: whoever starts the take names it, everyone records together, and releasing it releases it for the whole band. Its quality is the members' average plus 3 per extra member.
If one member runs out of goes, the take is scrapped for everyone.
If the host leaves, the room closes and the others carry on alone.
Emotes

Press B for the emote wheel: 👋 Wave · 🕺 Dance · 👏 Clap · 🙌 Cheer · 😂 Laugh · 🎸 Air guitar · 🌀 Spin · ❤️ Love.

Connection

Players connect browser to browser. When a direct link can't be made (school networks, strict mobile data), the game switches to a relay after 9 seconds, so everyone still shares one room.

References
^ 161-multiplayer.js. WaveFern source code, game v47.9.0.
Category: Multiplayer

Settings and graphics
From the WaveFern Wiki

Settings opens from the main menu or the pause menu. Under Graphics pick a preset or your own mix.[1]

The Graphics settings.
Preset	Pixel size	Frame cap	Crowds	Weather	Draw distance
High	3	none	all	full	normal
Medium	3	60	half	light	normal
Low	4	30	a quarter	off	near

Auto starts on High and steps down while the game runs slowly, remembering the level it settled on. Graphics settings are saved per device, never in your career.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/versions/

Version history
From the WaveFern Wiki

The game is on v49.19.0. This list is read live from the game, so it is always current.

Version	What changed
v49.19.0	The game is called just WaveFern again, on the title screen, loading screen, trailer end card, wiki and every page title. Page titles, descriptions and share previews now say what WaveFern is (a free music career game you play in your browser), and the share picture shows the new name.
v49.18.1	The game no longer names the 3D library it is built on: the "Made with" line is gone from the title screen, and the wiki credits, site description and notes no longer mention it. Nothing about how the game plays or looks changes.
v49.18.0	Trailer: the step captions are now one green strip with black text. Five steps: 1 Make your artist (longer, more looks), 2 Record songs (now the Lyrics step, always picking the rhyme), 3 Release them, 4 Gain fans, 5 Collab with artists (the meeting is two quick exchanges). The plaque cutscene moved after the millions of listeners, so the Billions Club plaque no longer comes before 50K.
v49.17.0	Trailer: the opening now shows how the game is played, one numbered step at a time with a caption: 1 Record songs (walk to the mic, pick a genre, hit the green), 2 Release them (upload on the laptop), 3 Gain fans (listeners counting up), 4 Collab with artists (message them, then meet and pick the replies they like best). The furniture shot is gone. Each plaque on the studio wall is named as it goes up (Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Billions Club, with its stream count).
v49.16.0	Trailer: the message is just "collab?" and the camera no longer zooms in on the reply. A new shot places furniture in your room, so the "How far can you go?" card is shorter. The plaques are now a cutscene of your studio wall, each one lifted into place on the hit. Instagrime gets floating hearts over the post, marked as non-gameplay footage.
v49.15.0	The game is now called WaveFern Studios (title screen, page titles, wiki and trailer end card). Trailer: the stage 4 to 1 festival run is now the game's own gameplay view, with the crowd growing on each stage. The message scene zooms in on the message as you type it, pulls back as you send, then zooms in on their reply, with quick smooth keyframes.
v49.14.1	Trailer: wavefern.com/trailer now goes straight to the Ready card (press Space to roll) instead of the scene menu. The menu is still at wavefern.com/trailer/?menu.
v49.14.0	Trailer: the opening is now the character, a first song (the Mix step), your first listeners, then you message an artist yourself (the chat starts empty, you ask to collab and they say yes), then the collab meeting. Naming yourself on Spotifly is gone. The plaques go up while you record alone in your studio, one a second. The Mix step is played like a person, reacting a moment late, drifting off the band and correcting, and the beat bar hits are a little early or late instead of dead centre.
v49.13.0	Trailer: the festival goes from the Fresh Fern Tent to The Pit, the Riverside Stage and the Main Stage, one stage a second on the beat, each seen from behind its crowd so you watch it grow. The messages shot follows the typing up close, then pulls back to show your message land and the artist reply (a reply written for the trailer). No car is in your lane when you drive and nobody is in your way when you walk. Cinematic camera shots carry a small Non-gameplay footage note, and the heavy setup before the drop now happens during the half second of black.
v49.12.1	Trailer: fixed the music glitching. The trailer used to jump the music to catch up with the picture when they drifted apart, and now the picture follows the music instead. The character randomizing is 2 seconds, the message is typed in full and only sent once it is written, with time to see it land and the reply start, and the pointer moves more slowly with a short pause before each click.
v49.12.0	Trailer: the new, longer soundtrack (1:44) is in, and the trailer is cut to it. The opening now runs 40 seconds so every early shot has room: the bedroom card, randomizing a character, $100 and a laptop, naming yourself, a first song, your first listeners, messaging an artist and the full collab meeting, then How far can you go? before the drop at 0:40. The breakdown is at 1:12, Tokyo at 1:16, the stadium at 1:24, black at 1:32 and the end card at 1:36.
v49.11.1	Trailer: the Internet is watching card is gone (the collab meeting gets its time), and the fades in and out of black before the drop are quicker so less of each shot is lost.
v49.11.0	Trailer: your rise is now gradual. Three Spotifly check-ins through the montage each pick up where the last left off (1K to 48K, 48K to 640K, 640K to 3.8M listeners, with followers and Fame Level climbing too), and the Instagrime post sits at 21K likes, so you have millions by the time you take it on tour. The drive and festival shots are shorter to make room.
v49.10.0	Trailer: the character creator now flicks through looks with the Randomize button (no pointer). The opening shows the climb from nothing: naming yourself, a first song in the studio (the Mix step), then your first 1,284 listeners and 37 followers counting up. The Money runs out card is gone, and How far can you go? is one card. When the music cuts out at 1:16 the picture snaps to black until the end card at 1:20.
v49.9.2	Trailer: the studio plaques go up once a second, on the hits, Gold to Billions Club, and the end card text lands on the beat, one line a second from 1:20.
v49.9.1	Trailer: the studio plaques now go up exactly on each beat (the game only rebuilt its plaque wall every 2 seconds, so the trailer puts up its own).
v49.9.0	Trailer: in the studio after the drop, a plaque goes up on the wall on every beat of the song, Gold to Platinum to Diamond to Billions Club, until the wall is full. The solo studio shot before the drop now plays the Mix step (holding the level in the green band) instead of the beat bar. The soundtrack is unchanged.
v49.8.0	Trailer review pass. The end card now says A music career game. Spotifly listeners and followers count up from zero to millions, and a new shot shows your single blowing up on Instagrime with likes counting up and comments rolling in. The setup cards now name real challenges: Money runs out. Rivals fire back. The internet is watching. The wardrobe, map and second city shots are cut and the festival gets the time. Text-heavy shots (naming yourself, messaging, Spotifly, Instagrime, World Tour) zoom in on the screen so they read on a phone.
v49.7.1	Trailer fixes: the cut from the Tokyo flyover to the stadium no longer flashes the airport street (it holds black for a moment, then the stadium slams in on the beat), and starting the trailer from a later scene uses the same character the creator scene makes.
v49.7.0	The first 24 seconds of the trailer now build suspense: short bursts of the start of a career (making your character, naming yourself, messaging an artist, meeting up, a first take) fade in and out of black between cards that set up the game and its challenges: Every star started in a bedroom. $100, a laptop, zero fans. Rent is due, rivals are climbing. The critics are watching. How far can you go? Then the beat drops on the city.
v49.6.0	The trailer now plays its own soundtrack, made for it at 120 BPM, and is retimed to it: the beat drops on the city at 0:24, Then take it on tour runs 0:56 to 1:00, the Tokyo flyover 1:00 to 1:08, the stadium show 1:08 to 1:20, and the end card lands on the final bit at 1:20. The artist in the trailer is called WaveFern. The own-music picker in the trailer menu is gone.
v49.5.0	Trailer polish. The beat now drops on a slow camera move over the city, with more cinematic shots mixed into the gameplay: Fern Road, the festival crowd, and a stadium camera that pushes in from the crowd and then rises over the show. Tokyo uses the real arrival flyover. Shots are cleaner, with no stray HUD, skip button or guards. Starting from a later scene gives you a styled character. You can load your own music in the trailer menu and set its BPM and drop time so the cuts land on your beat.
v49.4.0	The trailer moved to wavefern.com/trailer and is now real gameplay in the normal game camera: the title screen, making a character, picking an artist name, messaging an artist, the collab meeting and session, recording, Spotifly, the city, driving, the wardrobe, the Gphone, the map, a Main Stage festival set, the World Tour app, Tokyo and a stadium show, with plain title cards. A pointer clicks through the real menus. Track 1 plays over it with the beat dropping on the collab, and all game music and sounds are muted. It runs on a fresh career and saves nothing. The trailer save code is gone.
v49.3.1	Fixed trailer mode stuck on a black screen. Opened from the pause menu, the game stayed paused underneath so the trailer never started, and the Ready card telling you to press Space was hidden. The Ready card now shows, a click also rolls the trailer, and Esc on it takes you back to the menu.
v49.3.0	Trailer mode. Type trailer in the save code box (Settings > Save) to open a menu that plays a ready-made trailer of the game, about 80 seconds, for screen recording: cinematic shots of your own character in the bedroom, the studio, the city, the festival, the awards hall, the airport, Tokyo and a stadium show, with captions, motion graphics and the Rocket track. Play the whole thing or start from any scene, and turn music, captions, black bars or game sounds on or off. Your career is saved first, nothing is saved while trailer mode is on, and leaving brings your career back as it was.
v49.2.0	A deeper career. Make a song now has a Mood (Balanced, Hype, Chill, Emotional) and a Length (Radio, Short, Long) that shape how a song streams, its quality and the followers it wins; the 9 genres are unchanged. Songs that pass 1M, 10M, 100M and 1B streams earn Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Billions Club plaques, sent in the mail and hung on your studio wall. The Quests app has a Legacy tab with big late-game goals, your plaques and your music friends: collabs build bonds, friends charge less to collab and close friends share your new songs. 12 lost tapes are hidden on the city pavements and 3 street moments pop up every day. In a band room, every bandmate online adds 12% to your streams.
v49.1.0	Wardrobe fix and polish. Picking a colour in the wardrobe now recolours the clothes you have on straight away: the wardrobe never knew what the character creator dressed you in, so it only changed the card. Wardrobe cards now show you wearing each piece in the colour you pick, hats sit over your hair instead of it poking through, and the beret and headband sit properly. New settings in Settings > Game: camera zoom, always run, key hints, auto-pause and a 12-hour clock. The first days move faster (new artist buzz on streams until Fame Level 4), passing 100, 1K, 10K and more listeners, streams or followers gets a celebration, and a few one-time tips point new players at the map, Quests, Instagrime and the Gearshop. Smoother play: the HUD is no longer rebuilt every frame. Fixed the airport tutorial step never finishing.
v49.0.3	Fixed a player being teleported back into the Main Stage crowd at the festival field. An old one-off fix kept firing every time they started or reloaded a career; it is gone, so you now stay where you left off.
v49.0.2	No more hard cutoff for who can DM you: any artist can, but the bigger they are than you, the faster the chance drops. Someone about your size messages often, a star 10x bigger is rare, and a star like Doja Cat or Shawn Mendes (about 560M) messaging a 20M player is around 1 in 80,000 a day. At a handful of listeners it is so unlikely it will probably never happen.
v49.0.1	Big stars no longer DM you while you are still far smaller than them. An artist only messages you once you have at least a tenth of their monthly listeners, so someone like Doja Cat or Shawn Mendes waits until you are at about 56M, not 20M. You can still message anyone yourself.
v49.0.0	If you played at the old wavefern.github.io/WaveFern address, a card now tells you the game has moved to wavefern.com and that your saves came with you. The old address and anything under wavefern.github.io send you to wavefern.com.
v48.9.0	A new soundtrack track: Rocket. It plays in the background with the rest of the soundtrack, can be turned on or off and previewed in Settings, and is in the soundtrack player on the wiki Credits page. Your track on and off choices are kept.
v48.8.0	WaveFern has its own web address: play at wavefern.com and read the wiki at wavefern.com/wiki. The old wavefern.github.io/WaveFern link still works and sends you to the new one, and the first time you open wavefern.com your careers, backups and settings from the old address come with you.
v48.7.0	Pop-ups no longer pile on top of each other. Messages, release and goal cards, flight cards and tutorial cards all line up in one neat column at the top of the screen, below any bar that is showing there, with at most 5 at once. When the same pop-up comes up again while it is still on screen it shows a counter instead (x2, x3, x4...) and stays up a little longer. Floating reward pops step out of each other's way too.
v48.6.0	New sound effects. Clicks, pickups, purchases, wins, errors, doors and footsteps are now built from layers (a soft tap, a short wooden or glassy tone, a little room) and change slightly every time, so they feel less like beeps and do not get tiring. They sit a little quieter under the music. Footsteps alternate left and right and sound harder on indoor floors, the tutorial typing is a soft tick, night crickets sound more natural, and the music minigames have proper drum, bass, guitar, keys and pad sounds. A button that makes its own sound no longer plays a click on top.
v48.5.0	The wiki has screenshots: 29 pictures taken from the game, beside the text on the pages they belong to, with a gallery where a page has more than one. Click one to see it full size.
v48.4.0	You can play the whole soundtrack from the wiki Credits page. A player bar at the bottom has play and pause, previous and next, 10 second skips, a seek bar and volume, and keeps playing while you read other pages.
v48.3.0	The wiki Contact form now filters messages before sending: no swearing, slurs, threats, links, shouting or random letters, and one message every couple of minutes, up to 5 a day.
v48.2.1	The wiki soundtrack credit has new wording.
v48.2.0	The tutorial now teaches as you play. A new career only covers the basics (walk, pick a name, record, release), then Big Vee pops up the first time you reach something new: your first DM, the street, a car, a shop, being tired, the festival, a booked flight and the airport, a tour city and more. When a tip is about a place, a glowing guide line runs along the ground from you to it. The progress panel is gone, and tips can be turned on or off from the pause menu.
v48.1.1	The wiki Contact form is now open.
v48.1.0	The wiki has a Contact page with a form for sending a message to the people who make the game.
v48.0.0	The wiki has a new Frequently asked questions page with quick answers to the questions players ask most.
v47.9.1	The wiki now links to tumfy.net in the credits and on the page about how songs are made.
v47.9.0	The wiki credits the soundtrack (Rowan Burton, made in FL Studio with Surge XT, Arminator 2 and tumfy's free kits) and has a new page on how the songs you make are turned into music. Haggling styles and real artists are no longer listed in the wiki.
v47.8.0	Big Vee and the tutorial now say you pass out at 06:00, which is when it really happens. The wiki gets Tips on its main pages, a Credits page, a Secrets page, and a note on what Label HQ will be for.
v47.7.1	Making a song on a controller: the Beat, Lyrics and Mix steps now say which pad buttons to press, each lyric answer shows its button, and the D-pad can pick answers too. The beat hint is no longer replaced by the walking controls.
v47.7.0	The wiki has a plainer, encyclopedia-style look: a sidebar of links, Article, Source and History tabs, one green accent colour, plain boxes and bordered tables. Emoji icons, rainbow colours, pop-up rewards and scroll animations are gone. Links to pages you have read turn a darker green.
v47.6.1	Fixed the controls hint flickering between keyboard and controller: the controller text is now put in before the screen draws, and the game only switches back to keyboard prompts when you press a key or clearly move the mouse.
v47.6.0	The wiki now reads like an encyclopedia: Read, Source and History tabs on every page, a numbered Contents box, See also and References, page previews when you point at a link, and a Main Page with a featured article, In the news and Did you know. It is more fun too: pages you read are ticked off with a rank and a progress bar, new pages and rank-ups pop up with pixel confetti, sections slide in as you scroll, and a random page button.
v47.5.1	Controller prompts match your controller: PlayStation pads show ✕ ○ □ △, L1/R1, L2/R2, Share and Options; Switch Pro pads show their own letters, ZL/ZR and + / −; Xbox and other pads keep A B X Y.

v46.6.0	Band rooms now work on networks that block direct connections, such as many school networks. The relay only sends what changed and only sends positions of bandmates in the same area, so it stays inside the free Firebase limits. Everything that arrives from other players is now cleaned before the game uses it. Join a room can also find rooms through the relay. Saves still load.

v36.8.0	Song quality starts low and takes a long time to build. Every song you record is multiplied by an experience factor that starts at 30 percent and climbs with the songs you have recorded, the mentors you unlock and your fame level, so a new player makes poor songs and decent ones take roughly 150 songs. Weak songs also stream less. Going viral is now far rarer: about 0.03 percent per release at the best quality (it was 0.3 percent) and much lower for weaker songs. Saves still load.

v36.3.0	Weather. Each day now has its own weather, kept in your save so a reload never changes it. 9 days in 10 are sunny; the rest bring rain, fog or a thunderstorm with lightning. Shops and other interiors stay dry. The weather shows next to the time of day. Saves still load.

v30.8.1	Messages set-a-date panel now uses the Messages look (cream and plum, pink-to-violet buttons and chips) instead of the dark green default. Added docs/THEMES.md, a theme sheet for every app so new UI matches.
v30.8.0	Scheduled collabs, fair fees and smarter DMs. A collab no longer happens the moment you pay. You agree the fee, then pick a day, a time and a place (in Messages, or just type "friday at 3pm at the cafe", "tomorrow evening", "day 15"). The artist checks their own calendar and rules and yours: if they cannot do it they tell you why (rest day, other business, working hours, notice needed, how far ahead they will commit, a place they never go or only visit on certain weekdays, another session or festival slot) and suggest slots that work for both of you. Places on an artist's never list cannot be bargained into. Once agreed the session sits in your Calendar. Nothing is charged when you schedule (you just need the fee in your pocket); when the time comes, even if you slept through the day or loaded your game later, the money moves once, the artist turns up at the place and waits for 3 hours, and you walk up to them to record as before. Cancelling or moving more than a day ahead is free; under a day, cancelling costs 25% of the fee (plus 1 reputation) and moving costs 10%. Cancel while the artist is already waiting and you get 75% of a fee back (a payment you received goes back in full). If you never show, a fee you paid is lost, a payment you received is taken back, reputation drops by 2, the artist cools off for 5 days, and you are never charged twice. A finished collab gives +1 reputation and puts a release day in your calendar. One fee function now prices everything: small artists charge a modest fee that grows with their audience (about $6 at a handful of listeners, $35 for a 150-listener artist, a few hundred for 2,000), a bit more the bigger they are compared with you and a bit less for artists you have worked with or a good reputation; when they message you first they pay you a share of what your own audience is worth, never more than 80% of their own fee. Who messages you now depends on your size: artists about your size are the most common, slightly smaller ones frequent, slightly bigger ones occasional (more when you are growing), much smaller ones rare unless there is a reason (same sound, a past collab), and big stars rarely contact an unknown player, with the chance rising with your listeners, reputation and momentum. Genre fit, reputation and noise decide between similar artists. This applies on the first day too. Offers now come with the pay, the terms and a few dates to choose from.
v30.7.0	Calendar, weekdays and where artists will go. A free Calendar app is on your computer (it installs itself on old saves too, and is listed free in App Barn). It shows everything with a time in one place: scheduled sessions, festival sets booked in FestivalApp, release days and anything you add yourself (recording sessions, promo, other). Month view and day view, with a Show menu to look at an artist instead of yourself and see when they are free or busy (green and orange hours, rest days, other business, and the places they will not go). Each event shows its name, day, time, place, who is involved and any cost or earnings. You and the artists can never be in two places at once: events cannot overlap and need a travel gap between places, and festival bookings are checked against the calendar too (a festival slot is refused if you already have something then, and the other way round). Days now have weekdays: Day 1 is a Monday, so the festival is always on a Sunday. Every artist now has fixed habits generated from their name (nothing is stored): places they will never go (rappers always have at least one), places they only visit on certain weekdays, a rest day, working hours, how much notice they need and how far ahead they will commit. Acts on the festival stages no longer appear on stages or days their rules rule out, and collab songs in your festival setlist are checked too: a featured artist who is on another stage then, away on other business or never plays that stage cannot join, and you are told why. Events are saved in S.cal and in save codes.
v30.6.0	Negotiation with personality. Every artist now has their own way of haggling, fixed by their name so it is the same in every save: flexible, stubborn, proud, greedy, generous or shrewd. Counteroffers are no longer tiny steps. How far an artist moves depends on who they are, how big they are (big names move less), how well you know them, how far apart you are and how reasonable your offer is, so a big jump from you gets a big move back and a small one a small move. Prices round to sensible steps ($1, $5, $10, $25 and so on). An offer inside what the artist can live with is accepted with a chance that grows with how attractive it is and with every round, so deals usually happen but are never guaranteed. Lowball offers get shot down, proud artists walk away after two insults, everybody gives a final offer when they are tired of it, and walking away means no new offers from them for 4 days. Prices and phrases are read exactly as before, and cursing at an artist still gets you blocked.

v30.5.0	Outdoor ambience and cars with music. Outside, the world now has sound: it is busiest in the city centre and plaza (cars passing with a Doppler-style pitch and pan, horns, crowd chatter, footsteps), quieter on your home street (a few cars, birds, distant voices), and in Central Park it is birds, wind, far-off traffic and children near the playground. The festival grounds get a muffled crowd on festival days, and the quiet fields are just wind and birds. Nights are quieter, with crickets. It is all synthesised, follows the Effects slider and M, and fades out indoors, in the pause menu, the laptop and sleep screens. About a million cars live in this city: each car that drives past you is a draw, and with probability monthly listeners / 1,000,000 it is blasting one of your own released songs (muffled, bass-heavy, panned and louder as it comes closer). The soundtrack dips by 30% while one passes. Clips you drop in audio/cars/ can also turn up in passing cars (see the README there). The soundtrack itself is unchanged.
