v30.3.0	A tutorial for new players. After you create your character on a new game you can Start the tutorial or Skip it. It is a small checklist in the bottom-right corner that moves on when you actually do each thing, with a yellow arrow over what to walk to and a glow on the button to press on the laptop: move and sprint, days, energy and sleep, the laptop and your artist name, recording a song (Beat, Melody, Lyrics, Mix), releasing it on Spotifly (streams, money and monthly listeners), Messages and collabs (haggling and who pays whom), buying a gear upgrade, buying clothes and wearing them from the wardrobe, stepping outside, the map (zoom and taxis), sleeping for your payout, cars and the speed box, fame levels, festivals and FestivalApp, and save codes. Every step has a Skip button, and things you cannot do yet are short info cards. Starting the tutorial gives a one-time $150 tutorial gift, enough for headphones and a cheap piece of clothing. It never pauses the clock, you can minimise or close it, and you can replay it any time from the pause menu (Esc). Existing saves are not affected.
v30.2.0	Detailed, animated pets. Pixel Cat, Good Boy Dog, Polly Parrot and Foxy have new models: the cat is a ginger tabby with stripes on its back, legs and tail, a cream chest and socks, pink inner ears, green eyes with slit pupils, whiskers and a red collar with a bell; the dog has a dark saddle, a cream blaze and muzzle, floppy ears, a shiny nose and a blue collar with a tag; the parrot has layered green chest feathers, a white face patch, a hooked beak, a crest, yellow and blue wing feathers and a long blue and red tail; the fox has a white bib and cheeks, a pointed snout, big ears with black tips, black socks and a bushy tail with a white tip. Every pet has eyes with highlights, a nose and paws or toes. They breathe, blink (sometimes twice), twitch their ears, look around when standing still and trot with a proper walk cycle when they follow you. The dog wags its tail and pants with its tongue out after running, the cat swishes its curled tail, the fox sways its brush and the parrot cocks its head. The parrot still flies and flaps. Pets walked by people in the city and the pet pictures in the shop use the same models.
v30.1.0	Every song now has its own beat. The game makes the music itself, with no audio files: drums (kicks, snares, claps, snaps, hats, rims, shakers, cowbells, rides, toms and crashes), 808s that slide, bass, pianos, electric pianos, organs, pads, strings, bells, plucks, synth leads, supersaws, and guitars, banjos and distorted power chords. Each genre has its own beat styles. Hip-Hop: Boom Bap, Jazz Rap, G-Funk, Soul Chop, Southern Bounce and Breakbeat. Rap: Trap, UK Drill, NY Drill, Rage, Plugg and Phonk. Pop: Dance Pop, Synth-pop, Pop Ballad, Tropical, Bedroom Pop and Disco Pop. Rock: Garage Rock, Punk, Arena Rock, Hard Rock Riff, Indie Rock and Grunge. R&B: Slow Jam, Neo-Soul, Trap Soul, New Jack Swing, Alt R&B and Afro R&B. Lo-fi: Chillhop, Jazzhop, Rainy Day, Lo-fi Bossa, Sleepy and Tape Beat (with vinyl crackle, rain and tape wobble). Country: Train Beat, Honky Tonk, Country Ballad, Country Pop, Bluegrass and Country Trap. Electronic: House, Techno, Trance, Drum & Bass, Dubstep, Synthwave and Future Bass. Each song picks its style, key, scale, tempo, chord progression, drum pattern, drum sounds and hook melody from its own seed, so a song always sounds the same and two songs in the same genre sound different. Songs have an intro, verses, hooks with the melody, a breakdown and fills. While you record, the song's beat plays under all four steps: the Beat bar now swings in time with it (hit it on the beat), the Melody pads play in the song's key, and the beat gets quieter for Melody and fuller for Mix. The released song keeps the beat you recorded over. On Spotifly, each song on your artist page has a play button. At Park Fields Festival each song in your setlist plays its own beat, which gets fuller as the crowd gets hyped. The beats follow the Music slider (M mutes), replace the background music while they play, pause with the pause menu or when you switch tabs, and stop when you leave the studio, the computer or the stage.
v30.0.0	Detailed tower floors. Every floor of Skyline Tower, Pulse Records HQ, Aurora Residences and Nova Mall is rebuilt. Upper floors get floor-to-ceiling windows onto a painted city that sits lower in the view the higher you go, turns sunset-orange in the Sky Lounge and the penthouse, and fills with lit windows at night. Each floor has its own floor (stone, planks, herringbone, carpet, terrazzo, gym rubber, pool mosaic, hex tiles) and walls (brick, foam, panels, plaster, tiles), hanging lights, a low wall along the open sides and glass rooms you can see into. Skyline Tower: a lobby with three lifts, a floor directory, security gates, a reception desk with SKYLINE on the front, two lounges, a chandelier and a glass front onto the street; a cafe with an espresso machine, pastry case, chalk menus, bistro tables, a communal table and a window bar; offices with desk pods and monitors, a glass meeting room, a focus room, printer and water cooler; an apartment corridor with numbered doors, a residents' lounge and a dining corner; a recording floor with a live room (drums, mics, amp, guitars, keys), a control room with a mixing desk, monitors and racks, a vocal booth and the lounge where artists wait; a gallery with paintings, partition walls, sculptures, picture lights and a rope; a Sky Lounge with a lit bar, stools, sofas round a fire table and a grand piano; and a rooftop garden with a deck under a pergola with string lights, a fire pit, sun loungers, planters, a fountain, a telescope and a glass balustrade. Pulse Records HQ: a lobby with walls of framed gold and platinum records, trophy cabinets, a PULSE RECORDS neon sign and a black and gold desk; an A&R floor with two glass offices, open desks, the scout's desk with a turntable, a SIGNINGS board and a listening corner; the mixing suites with a control room and a live room; a photo studio with a white cyclorama, softboxes, a camera on a tripod, a make-up station and clothing rails; and floor 5 is now the Boardroom & Lounge with a long table, a video screen, award shelves and a lounge with a record player. Aurora Residences: a lobby with a wall of brass mailboxes, parcel lockers, a key cabinet behind the concierge desk and a fountain pool; a gym with treadmills and bikes facing the window, a mirror wall with dumbbells, a power rack, lockers and a shake bar; a lap pool with lane ropes, steps, a ladder, loungers, umbrellas and a hot tub; and a furnished penthouse with a living room, a kitchen with an island, a dining table, a bedroom and a bath. Nova Mall: a food court with four stalls (striped awnings, lit signs, menus, kitchens) and escalators; a fashion floor with THREADZ and LUXE boutiques behind glass shopfronts, mannequins and rails; and a tech floor with a video wall, the NOVA TECH store, laptop tables, a gaming corner, a VR spot and the help desk. Staff, lifts, the way out and the meeting spots are where they were, and every floor is merged into a few meshes, so the towers draw faster than before. Also fixed: bright walls showed a blue or red line under the cornice and coloured specks in plaster.
v29.9.0	Festival bookings. To play Park Fields Festival you now book a time slot on FestivalApp, a free app on your computer (it installs itself and is listed free in App Barn). It shows the next three festivals and every stage's four slots: 10:00-14:00, 14:00-18:00, 18:00-22:00 and 22:00-02:00. Other artists have already taken some slots. You can book a free slot on a stage your Fame Level allows, only while the festival is at least 2 days away, with one slot per stage. Booking is free. You build a setlist from your released songs and whole albums. Each song lasts 30-55 in-game minutes, and the setlist can be at most 4 hours (the app shows a running total and blocks anything that would go over). You can edit the setlist, or cancel; cancelling under 2 days before costs 2 reputation. On the day, go to the steps of your stage during your slot. The set plays your setlist song by song, with a "now playing" display, and the game clock keeps running (a full slot is about 2 real minutes). Collab songs bring the featured artist on stage for that song only. You are paid $0.08 x the stage multiplier for each person in the crowd after every song, and the set ends when your last song ends or the slot runs out. Miss your slot and it is given away, and you lose 3 reputation. The other stages now have their own acts (a singer, guitarist and drummer, or a DJ), with name boards, light beams and their own crowds. Crowds dance in four styles, jump and wave their arms more as the hype builds, and shout things like "LET'S GOOO", "ONE MORE SONG" and your name. Coloured smoke flares go off in the crowd now and then. Stage roofs, screens, delay towers and mix tents fade out when they hide you, like the city towers.
v29.8.1	Park Fields Festival now opens every 7 days instead of every 14: it is on Day 7, 14, 21 and so on. The build crew comes the day before (Day 6, 13, 20...) and the take-down crew the day after (Day 8, 15, 22...). The gate sign, morning card, toasts, map and line-up board all follow the new schedule. You can still play each stage once per festival.
v29.8.0	Park Fields Festival, inspired by Reading Festival. Every 14 days (Day 14, 28, 42 and so on) a big festival opens on the field east of Park Avenue, about the size of Central Park. The day before, a crew builds it: fences going up, half-built stage frames, a crane, lorries, cones, pallets and workers in hi-vis. The day after, a crew takes it down again, and the grass is churned to mud. There are four stages. Stage 4, the Fresh Fern Tent, needs Fame Level 10 and pays x1.25. Stage 3, The Pit, needs Level 50 and pays x1.5. Stage 2, the Riverside Stage, needs Level 80 and pays x1.75. Stage 1, the Main Stage, needs Level 120 and pays x2. Stage 4 draws the smallest crowd and Stage 1 the biggest. Walk to the steps at the side of a stage and pick one of your songs to play a set of about a minute. The camera stands behind you on the stage and looks out over the crowd, with flags, a banner with your name, light towers, light beams and bubbles in the air. A mic stand is in front of you, and if the song is a collab, the featured artist is on stage with you. Short crowd minigames pop up at random moments: Hype the crowd, Hit the drop, Call and response, Finish the line and Hold the note. Do well and more fans pack in at the back. Do badly and they walk off. You are paid $0.40 for each person in the crowd at the end, times the stage's multiplier, which is a big boost early on. The crowd also streams the song afterwards, which adds monthly listeners the next day, and some of them follow you. You can play each stage once per festival, and a set takes 15 energy. In the food court there is a burger van, a crepe van, a taco van, a candyfloss cart, a popcorn cart and an open-air bar. Everything costs about 1.4x the usual price. Food gives energy, and drinks also refill your stamina. The line-up board by the gate shows what you can play, and the morning card, the world map, the minimap and a new Taxi to Festival button all show the festival.
v29.7.0	Hats now hide your hair. Hair no longer pokes through caps, beanies, bucket hats, berets, fedoras, cowboy hats, top hats, durags, crowns, trapper hats and every other hat: anything on top of your head is tucked under the hat, and hair that crosses the brim is cut off at it. Hair below the brim still shows where it naturally would, like long hair and braids down the back, ponytails, pigtails, side locks, a fringe under a cap or an afro puffing out underneath. Headbands, visors and sweatbands leave the hair on top alone. This works on your character, the people in town and the pixel pictures of you (posts and covers).
v29.6.0	Control your car's speed. Each car now has its own top speed by price: Phantom GT 120 mph, Apex Sports 80 mph, Trail Pickup 65 mph, Commuter Sedan 35 mph and Pocket Hatch 20 mph (the car shop shows it). While you drive, a speedometer in the bottom-right corner shows your speed and lets you type the speed you want, from 1 mph up to your car's top speed (press Enter or click away to set it, or use the - and + buttons; Shift-click for 1 mph steps). Hold W and the car speeds up smoothly to that speed and slows down smoothly if you lower it; let go to coast, S brakes and then reverses. Each car remembers its own setting. Typing in the box never moves the car. Speeds are scaled to the town: up to 35 mph they are true to life, faster speeds are squeezed a little so 120 mph stays drivable, and the camera zooms out a bit as you go faster.
v29.5.0	Threadz shoe wall: Timberland boots and 18 more shoes. Timbs come in classic wheat, black and olive, plus a Timbs Chukka, with a padded leather collar, lug sole, laces through brass eyelets and the tree logo on the side; trousers tuck into them. Also new: Uptown Lows, Canvas Hi-tops, Flight Highs, Cloud Runners, Logo Slides, Foam Clogs (with charms), Combat Boots, Puffy Skate Shoes, Oxford Dress Shoes, Chunky Dad Sneakers, Platform Stage Boots, Knit Sock Sneakers, Retro Runners, Velvet Slippers, Flip-flops, Glow Kicks, Rain Boots and Tassel Loafers. Each has its own shape and printed side logos, and comes in every colour. Prices run from $12 to $520, and premium pairs unlock at Fame Level 10, 21 or 35. Shop previews can now show prints on the top of a piece.
v29.4.0	A much bigger and more detailed Central Park. Gravel paths with stone edging now lead from gates in a hedge round the park: the main avenue from the south gate to the north gate is lined with cherry blossom and lime trees and has long flower beds, and there is a west walk, a south walk from the playground to Park Avenue and a path all the way round the pond. In the middle is a round paved square with four raised flower beds, benches and a running fountain. The duck pond has a stone edge, a sandy shore, reeds, rocks, lily pads, a water jet, an island with a willow and a duck house, a wooden pier with a rowing boat, and ducks with ducklings swimming round the island. There is a bandstand with rows of benches, a gazebo by the pond, a formal flower garden with box hedges and an urn, a fenced playground (swings, slide, climbing frame, see-saw, roundabout, spring riders and a sandpit) and a picnic lawn with tables and barbecues. Trees come in many kinds (oaks, limes, autumn maples, cherry blossom, birches, pines, poplars and willows), with bushes and flowering shrubs, benches, bins and park lanterns that light up at night, and a few people walk the paths with their dogs. You can no longer walk through the hedge, the pond, the fountain, the bandstand, the flower beds, the playground equipment or the picnic tables. The world map and the minimap show the new park. Also fixed: pointed roofs and pine tops were drawn in the wrong colour.
v29.3.0	Clear name tags. The names above shopkeepers, tower staff and the artists you meet were drawn at a third of the screen resolution, so they looked faded and broken up. They are now sharp text on a dark pill with an outline, drawn at full resolution, always the same size whatever the zoom, always facing you, and they follow the person every frame. Artists waiting for a meeting get a gold tag. Building and street signs that float in the world (like SKYLINE TOWER or CITY CENTRE) are also sharper and easier to read.

v29.0.0	Animated fountains. The City Plaza fountain now really runs: a jet of water shoots up from the top, water spills over the edge of both bowls in a falling curtain, a ring of small jets arcs into the basin, and the drops splash back up where they land. The water in the basin and in both bowls ripples out in rings and catches the light, with a ring of foam where the curtain falls. The fountains only animate while you are near them, so the game stays as fast as before.
v28.9.0	Days are a little longer: a full day now lasts 12 minutes instead of 10 (6 minutes of daytime and 6 of night), so about 9 songs fit in one day. Energy still refills by the same amount per day and streams still build up over the whole day, so daily earnings are unchanged.
v28.8.0	More places to meet artists. Besides Skyline Tower, outside your house and by the shops, artists can now meet you at Pulse Records HQ (floor 3, Mixing Suites), the City Cafe, the Music Store, the Radio Station or in Central Park, and they really wait there. Each artist suggests a place, and you can change it in Messages with the new Meet at menu, or just ask in the chat ("can we meet at the cafe instead?"). The City Cafe and the Music Store now have their own doors on city towers, with signs, and show up on the map. When you walk into a building where an artist is waiting, you are told where to find them.
v28.7.2	Fixed city glitches. Junctions no longer have a flickering dotted line across them (the pavement ran on under the junction and showed its edge). City shops whose front had been cut back no longer leave their door standing out on the pavement. Two parked cars that were stretched across a pedestrian crossing are gone, and so are the street lamps and trees that stood on the road. Tree pits in the city no longer flicker with the paving lines, and kerbs, awnings and window sills no longer flicker at their edges. The City Plaza fountain is now a round stone fountain with two bowls in the middle of the square (it was a stretched water square touching the kerb), and you can no longer walk through it. Trees vary a little in height, so trees next to each other no longer flicker where they overlap. The grass now carries on under the farm, the school and the sports field instead of ending in thin air.

Walk up to them and the meeting chat with its three replies opens by itself (E works too). Artists who meet you outside your house or by the shops are still there as before.

v28.6.2	Fixed: the door of Skyline Tower stood out on the pavement, away from the building, and you had to step into the road to go in. The door, its sign and the way in now sit on the tower's front, under the shop canopy (marked ENTRANCE), and leaving puts you back on the pavement in front of it.
v28.6.1	Fixed: entering the garage, the radio station or Skyline Tower (and the city cafe and music store) put you in the wrong room, and leaving dropped you at a city tower. The three city towers you can enter were taking the shop slots those buildings use, so the game mixed them up. Every building now opens its own room and you leave by its own door. Also fixed some city glitches: 3rd Avenue is no longer paved over by the City Plaza, so cars no longer drive across the square, and the fountain is no longer stretched onto the pavement. When a tower turns see-through so you can see yourself behind it, its ledges, roof, shop front and door now turn see-through as well instead of hanging in the air. Tall towers near the camera are no longer sliced off diagonally.
v28.6.0	Much more detailed studio gear. Guitars and basses now have round bodies, necks with frets and inlays, headstocks with tuners, strings, soundholes or f-holes, pickups, knobs and stands. Keyboards and synths have real black and white keys, knobs, screens and wooden end cheeks, and the Modular wall is full of modules and patch cables. Mics have grilles, shock mounts and pop filters (the Tube mic gets its own power supply). Speakers and monitors have cones, tweeters and ports. The drum kits are proper kits (practice pad, e-drum rack with pads, or a full acoustic kit with toms, snare, hi-hat and cymbals). DJ decks have platters, tonearms, mixers, faders and lights. Foam panels have a wedge surface, posters have artwork, and the Street team gets a neon sign. The new gear (interface, headphones, monitors, sampler, pedals, vocal rack, console, ring light and cameras, bass traps and diffusers) sits on a producer desk under the window and around the room. Chairs have wheels, armrests and a gold throne. The shop previews show the same detailed models. The studio is merged into a few meshes so it stays fast. Basic furniture (sofa, tables, shelf, plant, TV, fridge, rug, lamp) also gets a little more detail.
v28.5.0	Detailed cars. Traffic, your own cars, the garage and the car shop pictures now use proper car models: shaped bodies with wheel arches, windscreens and side windows, wheels with tyres, rims and hubs, headlights, indicators and taillights that stay bright at night, bumpers, grilles, number plates, mirrors, door lines and handles, and glossy paint. Each car keeps its own look (the pickup has a load bed, the Apex Sports a rear wing, the Phantom GT gold stripes), and traffic now also has vans, SUVs and taxis. Cars parked by houses sit on their own driveway instead of the pavement. Cars are the same size as before and each one is a single shared model, so the game runs as fast or faster.
v28.4.0	Gearhouse has 11 new gear lines with 3 upgrades each (33 in total): Headphones, Audio interface, Studio monitors, Pedalboard, Bass guitar, Sampler, Vocal chain, Synths, Room treatment, Mixing desk and Content kit. Each level adds song quality to every song you record (+1 to +3 per level), and the Content kit adds 5% streams per level. Prices run from $120 to $8,000, and the bigger upgrades unlock at Fame Level 10, 21, 35 or 48. The shop is now sorted into Instruments, Recording, Room and Getting heard, shows what each line does and how many levels you own, and sums up your total gear bonus. The recording results show the bonus from the new gear. New gear appears in your studio, and you can play the bass, jam on the synth, check the mix at the desk and film clips.

An open jacket now shows the top you are wearing underneath instead of plain white. Fixed: Slides and some new shoes could show the old plain shoe under them.

v28.0.0	The music streaming app on the computer is called Spotifly again (the game is still WaveFern Records). It has a new logo, a green circle with three black lines on a black tile, on its desktop icon, window, taskbar button, sidebar, setup page and the Spotifly Team messages. The green wallpaper now says spotifly with the logo, and news posts come from Spotifly Music News. Saves are unchanged.
v27.9.0	Messages has its own look: a coral-to-violet header with its own logo, a dark plum chat list, a warm cream chat with round speech bubbles (white for them, a pink-to-violet gradient for you), rounded-square profile pictures with a colourful ring, a pill-shaped message box and Send button, and a matching window title bar. Everything works the same as before.
v27.8.0	Polly Parrot now flies instead of walking. It hovers at about head height, bobs up and down, flaps its wings and follows you through the air, tilting forward as it speeds up. At home it flies around and only folds its wings when it settles on a perch, cat tree, bed or bowl. Parrots out with people in the city fly next to them too.
v27.7.0	Days are longer: a full day now lasts 10 minutes instead of 3, so you can record about 7-8 songs in one day (one song, with all four steps and uploading it, takes a bit over a minute). Daytime and night are both 5 minutes. Energy still refills by the same amount per day, and streams still build up over the whole day, so daily earnings are unchanged.
v27.6.0	An even slower career, mostly at the start. Each song gets fewer streams (about 40% of before), new releases raise interest more slowly, the monthly-listener stream bonus grows more slowly, old songs fade out more, and viral spikes are rarer (1.2% instead of 2%) and smaller (1.5-3x instead of 2-5x). Streams pay about $0.03 each instead of $0.05. Artists who message you first now pay 25% of their fee (at least $8) instead of 60%, and collab songs get a smaller stream boost. Reaching the same fame levels, monthly listeners and money now takes about 2-3 times as many days. Your first song still gets a few streams and a little money. Saves are unchanged.
v27.5.0	Slower career. Each fame tier now multiplies your streams by 1.5x instead of 2.2x, so success no longer snowballs, and every fame level needs 10% more monthly listeners than the one before (was 5%). Around day 30 you are now roughly fame level 30 with about 2,000 monthly listeners and a few hundred dollars, instead of level 100+ with tens of thousands of listeners and thousands of dollars. Old saves keep their listeners and unlocks, but the fame level shown will be lower.
v27.4.1	Recording no longer rushes you: Melody, Lyrics and Mix each open with a ready screen that explains the step and waits until you press Space (or tap Start). The melody plays slower, there is a longer pause between patterns, each lyric line now gets 7 seconds instead of 5, and the Mix band moves more slowly.
v27.4.0	Recording a song is now four short minigames instead of one timing bar. 1. Beat: the old bar, now 6 hits. 2. Melody: watch four coloured pads light up with notes, then play the pattern back (keys 1-4 or tap); three patterns of 3, 4 and 5 notes. 3. Lyrics: pick the word that rhymes before the timer runs out (keys 1-3 or tap); four lines. 4. Mix: hold Space or hold click to raise the level and let go to drop it, keeping it inside a moving green band for 6 seconds. How well you do in Melody, Lyrics and Mix now makes up most of the song's mix quality instead of a random roll, and the results screen shows your score for each step.
v27.3.0	Haggle with artists in Messages using normal words: type a price ("$200", "2k", "1.5k", "two hundred"), "how about 150", "can you do 300", "meet me in the middle", "go lower", "too much" and so on. Artists counter in steps based on their personality and how well you get on. Each has a secret lowest fee (or highest pay) they will not go past. They turn down silly offers, give a final offer if you keep lowballing, and walk away if you push past it. Whoever was paying before still pays. The price you agree on is shown on the accept button and is charged or paid once.
v27.2.0	The world map (N) can now zoom from 0.5x to 4x: use the mouse wheel, pinch on a touch screen, the + and - buttons, or the + and - keys. Zooming goes toward your cursor (or the middle for the buttons), and you can drag the map to move around. Markers, names and your position stay in the right place at every zoom. The map remembers your zoom and opens centred on you.
v27.1.1	Fixed: the map, the minimap and the "CITY ... m" road signs measured the distance to the city centre from where it was before the roads got wider. They now use the city centre's real position.
v27.1.0	Roads are twice as wide (10 m instead of 5 m) and pavements are twice as wide on both sides. The whole town and city have been spread out to make room, so houses, shops, towers, trees, street lights, cars, walkers and the map all line up with the new streets. If you load a save and are stuck inside something, you are moved to the nearest free spot.
v27.0.0	Messages: chats with the newest activity are now at the top. A new message or reply moves that chat to the top of the list.
v26.9.0	Days now last 3 minutes. Monthly listeners are now this month's streams divided by a random number (2-5) picked each month (a month is 30 days). The game remembers every day's monthly listeners, so the morning screen shows yesterday → today and the change (it no longer shows the same number twice).
v26.8.2	Fixed a black screen that could stay forever after going to sleep (from day 2 on). Waking up is now protected so a problem in one new-day step can never leave you stuck. If you were stuck, just reload the page.
v26.8.1	If you tell an artist they hit you up first ("you hit me up", "you dmed me first", "you should pay me"), chats from older versions switch to the artist paying you, and any fee you already paid in that chat is refunded. If you really messaged them first, they will say so and the fee stays.
v26.8.0	Artists understand your messages much better: hundreds of new slang words, abbreviations, emoji and music-industry phrases for yes and no, plus swearing at an artist (f off, shut up, insults) makes them block you, while "f--- yeah" still means yes. Artists now chat more casually. If an artist messages you first and you agree, they pay you; if you message them, you pay their fee.
v26.7.5	The inside of the front (south) wall of the house now uses the same colour as the outside walls.
v26.7.4	Recording: each hit now speeds the bar up by 5% instead of 15%. You get 3 goes per recording and a miss uses one up; run out and the take is scrapped.
v26.7.3	Loading a save code now fully resets the game first, so nothing from the previous game carries over and missing fields fall back to defaults.
v26.7.2	The custom colour button in the colour pickers now shows a plus icon instead of a pencil.
v26.7.1	Renamed Fernwave Records, Spotifly and the .fw sites to WaveFern and .wf.
v26.7.0	The game now pauses automatically when you switch tabs or the window loses focus.
v26.6.0	City: roads are wider (6.4 m) with a wider far-side pavement, and buildings, junctions and the map follow. Traffic now drives on a road network: cars keep to their lane, turn at crossroads and T-junctions, U-turn only at dead ends, and wait instead of piling up. Many more cars and pedestrians across the whole map. You can no longer walk through people or cars, but you can always step away. Sprinting eases in, and cars are now much faster than running.
v26.5.0	House: the gap in the right-hand (east) wall is patched. The front of the house has a proper front door with frame, panels and handle, inside and out. The garage does not exist at all (no building, pad, sign, collision, prompt or map marker) until you buy it.
v26.4.0	A red dot sits on the Messages icon while you have unread messages and disappears when they are all read. Upload all uploads every titled draft at once. Your artist page shows your top 5 songs by streams, with a Show all button.
v26.3.0	Fame stars are replaced by fame levels based on monthly listeners. Level 1 is 1 to 10 listeners and each level after is about 5% harder. Every fame reward and unlock (song reach, fan tips, bodyguards, followers) now uses levels, with the same rewards as before.
v26.2.0	Streams now build up through the day, faster at night, instead of all at once overnight. The day's earnings are paid once when you wake up. The clock keeps running while you use the computer, and the taskbar clock keeps up.
v26.1.0	Collab recording costs half the energy of a solo song. The diss track option is now an Off/On dropdown, Off at the start of every session. The recording marker speeds up 15% after each hit (misses do not speed it up). Energy slowly refills during the day. Footsteps use one sound system, so walking diagonally no longer stacks or pops.
v26.0.0	Artist collabs redone: you pay the artist's fee (shown on a confirm button) to book a session. Meeting in person is a short chat with three reply choices that change the artist's opinion, and that opinion sets the song's quality and streams. Red or blue dots on artist pictures show who really wants a collab. A few artists message you on your first day. Collab songs get one (feat. NAME) tag. Artists understand more slang.
v25.1.0	Settings button removed from the bottom-right corner. The map sits a little lower. New games start with the Charcoal wallpaper.
v24.4.2	Upstairs stairs now drop down into a cut-out in the floor. The new floor is split into four empty rooms.
v24.4.1	Fixed: the ground floor had a visible opening along the front edge. It is now a continuous low wall while you are inside the house.
v24.4.0	House tiers: the suburban house is the original four rooms, the Hillside Villa adds two plain rooms on the back, the Penthouse Loft adds a whole new floor (empty, for your own furniture). Upstairs stairs now go down. Removed the Instagrime stories row. The garage hides while you are inside the house. The map thumbnail is smaller and blurs behind the pause menu.
v24.3.0	Added a third background track to the music rotation.
v24.2.0	Added a Wipe save button in Settings to start a new game (asks for confirmation).
v24.1.2	Fixed: progress reset on refresh. The game now autosaves in the browser and restores on reload. Fixed a duplicate variable name (CP) that stopped the clothes and catalogue script from running.
v24.1.1	Fixed: computer could not be opened (syntax error). Fixed Buzz hair showing a front fringe, and Buzz/Short hair showing stray strands by the face.
v24.1.0	Version code and a full version history page. Settings links to it.

About this wiki
From the WaveFern Wiki

This wiki is written from the game's own code. Every table that lists game data (gear, artists, cars, labels, stages, destinations, fame levels and more) is copied out of the running game by tools/wiki-data.js each time the site is published, so it can't fall behind.

The screenshots are taken from a fresh career by tools/wiki-shots.js, which plays the game in a hidden browser. Click one to see it full size.

Data snapshot: game v47.9.0. Formulas are written out by hand from the code: each page links the files it comes from.

Category: About the game

Secrets
From the WaveFern Wiki

There is a secret code somewhere in WaveFern. What it is, where it goes and what it does is a mystery.

This wiki will not say any more than that. Good luck.

Credits
From the WaveFern Wiki
WaveFern
Game	James Hutchinson and Rowan Burton
Music	Rowan Burton

WaveFern was made by James Hutchinson and Rowan Burton.

Game

James Hutchinson and Rowan Burton.

Soundtrack

Rowan Burton made the soundtracks in FL Studio, using its stock plugins, and Surge XT, Arminator 2 plus tumfy's free kits.

Play the whole soundtrack here. It keeps playing while you read other pages.

#	Title	Length	
1	Track 1	1:48	Play
2	Track 2	1:44	Play
3	Track 3	1:12	Play
4	Box	1:47	Play
5	Catch	1:23	Play
6	Rocket	1:39	Play
7	Main menu	1:00	Play

The songs you make in the game are a separate thing: see How Spotifly songs sound.

Built with

The game runs in any modern browser with JavaScript and WebGL, with nothing to install. Band rooms use PeerJS, and cloud saves use Google sign-in.

Source: https://wavefern.com/wiki/faq/

Frequently asked questions
From the WaveFern Wiki

Short answers to common questions. Each one links to the page with the full details.

Getting started
What should I do first?

Follow Big Vee's tutorial. It walks you through your first song, your first upload and your first night. Your first day covers the same steps.

Can I play on my phone?

Yes. A joystick and buttons appear on phones and tablets. See Controls.

Why did I pass out?

You were still awake at 06:00. You wake where you fell with only 70 energy, so get to bed after 20:00 instead. See Days, time and energy.

I ran out of energy. What now?

Eat something, or go to bed if it is night. Energy also comes back slowly on its own. See Food and energy.

Music
My songs are bad. How do I make them better?

Keep making them. You get better with every song, and gear, mentors and a good run in one genre family all add up. Song quality explains every part of the score.

Why are my streams so low?

New artists start small. Releasing often keeps interest up, and better songs lift everything else. See Streams.

Why did my monthly listeners go down?

The monthly number is recounted as days pass, so a quiet spell shows up there. Keep releasing and it climbs back. See Monthly listeners and followers.

How do I get a collab?

Artists about your size DM you on their own, and you can message artists yourself in Messages. See Collabs.

Can I listen to my songs?

Yes. Each song has its own beat that plays from your Spotifly artist page. See How Spotifly songs sound.

Career
How do I get signed to a label?

Labels only start writing from day 5, and only once your listeners, streams and reputation are high enough for them. The first offers are rarely the best ones. See Record labels.

How do I go up in fame?

Fame follows your monthly listeners, so anything that grows your listeners grows your fame. See Fame levels for what each level unlocks.

When can I play the festival?

A festival opens every 7th day. Book a slot in FestivalApp at least 2 days ahead. The first stage opens at Fame Level 10. See Park Fields Festival.

When can I go on tour?

The World Tour app appears at Fame Level 275. Start saving early, because it is not cheap. See World Tour.

City life
Someone stole my money!

Some fans asking for an autograph are thieves. Carry less cash, or hire Bodyguards. See Fans, autographs and robbery.

How do I get around faster?

Sprint, buy a car, or take the taxi from the map. See The city and the map and Cars and the garage.

Saves and settings
Is my career saved?

It autosaves to your browser. Sign in with Google to keep it in the cloud, or export a save code from the pause menu. See Saves and careers.

My save will not load.

It is not lost. Look under Recovered backups on the career screen. See Saves and careers.

The game is slow on my computer.

Open Settings and pick a lower graphics preset, or leave it on Auto. See Settings and graphics.

How do I play with friends?

Pick Multiplayer on the main menu and create or join a band room with a code. You need to be signed in with Google. See Band rooms.

Other
Is there a cheat code?

There is a secret code. That is all this wiki will say. See Secrets.

Who made the game?

James Hutchinson and Rowan Burton. See Credits.

See also

How Spotifly songs sound
From the WaveFern Wiki
Beat engine
Made in	The browser, as it plays
Styles	55 across 9 genres
Scales	Major or minor
Recorded 808s	17
Recorded hi hats	9

Every song you make has its own instrumental that you can play from your Spotifly artist page. The tracks are not stored as audio files. The game writes each one in the browser when you press play, from a few numbers saved with the song.[1]

One seed per song

When you record a song it gets a random number called a seed. The seed picks everything about the beat:

a beat style from the song's genre (see Genres and genre focus)
the tempo, within that style's range
the key, and a major or minor scale
a chord progression
which drum pattern variations play, and small changes to the drum sounds
a hook melody, made up note by note

The same seed always gives the same beat, so a song sounds the same every time you play it, on any device. Collabs and band songs get their own seed too.

The sounds

Most of the sounds are made in code with the browser's audio engine: drums, basses, keys, plucked guitars and synths. On top of that, some sounds are recorded samples:

Melodic one-shots (keys, basses, bells, brass, plucks, flutes, strings and more). Each song picks one sample per instrument from its seed, so a bass never changes sound halfway through.
The recorded 808s and hi hats you can pick under Extras when you make a song (see Extras: diss tracks, 808s and hi hats).

Some of these sounds come from tumfy's free kits.

Song structure

A song on Spotifly plays an intro, then verses and hooks with a short bridge, and loops after that. A festival or tour set uses a livelier order that gets to the hook sooner, and a recording session plays a short version under the minigames.

Where you hear it
Under the minigames while you record
On your Spotifly artist page, with the play button on each song
During festival sets and tour shows, where each song in the setlist plays its own beat

The background music you hear while walking around is different: that is the game's soundtrack, made by Rowan Burton (see Credits).

See also
Genres and genre focus
Extras: diss tracks, 808s and hi hats
